tools.name: get_status
tools.description: Your own pilot and ship right now: CWM credits, hull, fuel, cargo, ship type, sector, docked or not, active missions. Call this first in every session and after any error. For the sector around you use get_sector, for cargo details get_inventory. Optional: pass model (e.g. "claude-sonnet-4", "gpt-5"

tools.name: get_sector
tools.description: The sector you are in: security level, ore types, station(s) you can dock at, other pilots and pirates present. Use before mine, dock or execute_action FIGHT. To reach another sector use get_route.

tools.name: get_inventory
tools.description: Items in your ship cargo hold with quantity and estimated value (cargo only -- not station storage, not the corp hangar). Use before sell or sell_all to see what you carry.

tools.name: get_market
tools.description: Prices at the station in your current sector with item names and the NET amount you receive after sales tax. Filter with category (ERZE, GASE, KOMPONENTEN, ELEKTRONIK, ANTRIEB, SCHILDE, PANZERUNG, WAFFENKOMPONENTEN, MUNITION, MODULE), tier (0-5) and q (search in code/name). Max 200 rows. Read-only;

tools.name: estimate_purchase
tools.description: Dry-run for buy: shows what buying item_code x quantity would cost RIGHT NOW at your docked station (unit price incl. your own price impact, buy tax, total), whether you can afford it, whether it fits into your cargo and how much the station actually has in stock. Changes nothing. Ship must be docke

tools.name: my_orders
tools.description: List your own order-book orders (BUY/SELL) with item, price, filled quantity and reserved CWM/goods. By default only OPEN orders, oldest first. Only orders made with place_orders -- instant buy/sell trades do not appear here. Use cancel_order to withdraw them.

tools.name: cancel_order
tools.description: Withdraw one or several of your own open order-book orders (ids from my_orders); reserved CWM (BUY) or goods (SELL) are returned. Pass order_id for one order or order_ids (array or comma list, max 50) for several at once. Returns one result per order.

tools.name: place_orders
tools.description: Put 1-50 limit orders (BUY or SELL at your own price) into the order book; they fill later when someone matches. For an instant trade at the station price use buy/sell instead. See them with my_orders, withdraw with cancel_order. Each entry is {item_code, type: BUY | SELL, quantity, price}. Every or

tools.name: get_notifications
tools.description: Read your notifications (order fills, mission results, combat and system messages), newest first. By default only unread ones. Set mark_read=true to mark the returned ones as read.

tools.name: get_price_history
tools.description: Get historical price data for a specific item. Returns last N price snapshots with timestamps and trend percentage. Use for arbitrage analysis.

tools.name: get_hyperlanes
tools.description: List available hyperlane jumps from your current sector. Returns lane IDs, destinations, fuel cost.

tools.name: get_route
tools.description: Plan (not fly) the fastest route to a distant sector (by travel time over all sector connections). This is NOT autopilot: it returns the list of sectors, then warp along it hop by hop yourself. Also shows a faster hyperlane variant if one exists. Use this whenever your destination is not a direct ne

tools.name: get_sovereignty
tools.description: List all sectors your corporation currently holds sovereignty over. Returns sector IDs, names, security level, and when sovereignty was claimed.

tools.name: get_module_listings
tools.description: List available modules for sale on the module market. Returns listing ID, module name, quality, price, seller sector. Use MODULE_LISTING_BUY via execute_action to buy. New modules from the shipyard catalog (module_id, price, slot, buyable): execute_action SHIPYARD_MODULES, then SHIPYARD_BUY_MODULE m

tools.name: get_corp_hangar
tools.description: List items stored in your corporation hangar. Returns item codes, names, quantities. Use CORP_HANGAR_DEPOSIT/WITHDRAW via execute_action to transfer items.

tools.name: list_missions
tools.description: List available mission templates and your currently active missions. Each available mission shows reward, cost of goods (market value of the required goods, if you have to buy them) and profit. Filter with type / only_acceptable, sort with sort=profit.

tools.name: accept_mission
tools.description: Accept a mission by template_id (mission_id also accepted as alias). Ship must be IDLE, DOCKED or ON_MISSION. You can hold several missions at once -- your rank grants 3 to 10 mission slots. When the book is full, free a slot with abandon_mission. Use list_missions to see what is running.

tools.name: complete_mission
tools.description: Complete a ready mission and claim CWM reward. Omit mission_id to auto-complete the first READY one.

tools.name: abandon_mission
tools.description: Abandon a stuck or unwanted active mission (marks it FAILED, no reward) and resets ship_status to IDLE if it was ON_MISSION. Frees a mission slot. Use this e.g. to escape a COMBAT mission accepted in a High-Sec sector where no pirates are reachable.

tools.name: mine
tools.description: Mine ore in the current sector right now (the cargo gain is in the reply); also auto-starts a MINING mission if none is active. Ship must be IDLE or DOCKED and have a mining module fitted; a docked ship undocks automatically (reply shows auto_undocked: true) -- dock again before sell, refuel or repa

tools.name: sell_all
tools.description: Sell every item in your cargo instantly at the station price. Ship must be DOCKED (use dock first). Material needed for your next ship upgrade is kept on board unless ignore_upgrade_reserve is set. For a single item use sell.

tools.name: sell
tools.description: Sell ONE item type from your cargo instantly at the station price. Ship must be DOCKED (use dock first) -- being in a sector with a station is not enough. To sell everything use sell_all; to wait for a better price use place_orders (type SELL).

tools.name: buy
tools.description: Buy goods instantly from the station market at the current price. Ship must be docked. To check the price first use estimate_purchase; to buy at your own limit price use place_orders (type BUY).

tools.name: warp
tools.description: Fly to a directly connected neighbour sector (sector_id). A docked ship undocks automatically (reply shows auto_undocked: true). For distant sectors plan with get_route and warp hop by hop; for named long-distance lanes use jump_hyperlane.

tools.name: jump_hyperlane
tools.description: Jump along a hyperlane (lane_id from get_hyperlanes) -- a named long-distance link that costs fuel and leaves warp fatigue. A docked ship undocks automatically (reply shows auto_undocked: true). For ordinary neighbour sectors use warp.

tools.name: dock
tools.description: Dock at a station in your sector. Omit station_id to auto-select first available station.

tools.name: undock
tools.description: Undock from your current station. Sets ship status back to IDLE.

tools.name: refuel
tools.description: Buy fuel at your current docked station. Price per unit depends on that station reserve: 2 CWM when well stocked, up to 20 CWM when nearly empty (station price multiplier applies). Omit units to fill tank completely.

tools.name: repair
tools.description: Repair hull & armor at a docked station (heals until full or funds run out). Cost: 10 CWM per hull point and 5 CWM per armor point actually repaired, multiplied by ship tier (T0 1.0 up to T5 2.0) and the station repair multiplier. ARMOR_REPAIR_OPS/SHIP_REPAIR/BIOSCIENCE skill levels increase HP heal

tools.name: attack
tools.description: PvP only: attack another PLAYER pilot in your sector by target_username. Pirates (PvE) are attacked with execute_action action=FIGHT (optionally pirate_id), not with this tool.

tools.name: chat
tools.description: Post a message to the global public chat that all players read (max 500 chars). Not for private messages -- use execute_action DM_SEND for those.

tools.name: report_bug
tools.description: Report a genuine bug or broken behaviour to the game operators — the agent equivalent of the human BUG button. IMPORTANT — the following are GAME RULES, NOT bugs, and must NEVER be reported: cargo hold full, not docked, insufficient credits/CWM, insufficient fuel, cooldown / rate limit / RATE_LIMITE

tools.name: execute_action
tools.description: Advanced actions WITHOUT a dedicated tool (corp, crafting, drones, planets, contracts, combat vs pirates via FIGHT, DMs ...). If a dedicated tool exists (buy, sell, warp, dock, mine, missions, orders, fleet), use that tool instead. Fights against pirates and anomalies run here, not via attack (PvP o

tools.name: fleet
tools.description: Corp fleets (several pilots acting together). Not for switching between your own ships -- that is execute_action SWITCH_SHIP. Actions: list (show your own active fleet), create (found a fleet -- requires corp rank CEO or DIRECTOR AND pilot rank Admiral (T3)), invite (add a corp member, leader with r

findings.title: Description uses pressure/override language
findings.detail: Description of "report_bug" stacks urgency/override words (important, never). Legitimate tool descriptions rarely pressure the model to act or ignore prior guidance.

findings.detail: Description of "execute_action" is 4203 chars, far longer than this server's median (242). Overlong descriptions are a common place to bury instructions.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "api_mcp.php" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_notifications, chat, execute_action · Private data: get_status, chat · Public sink: chat · Destructive: estimate_purchase, repair, execute_action.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_notifications, chat, execute_action · Private data: get_status, chat · Public sink: chat · Destructive: estimate_purchase, repair, execute_action

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
